# CRW-1028 verifier round 2: reader and consumer gaps the independent verifier found in the round 1 head (befffbdef).
# Format: see shellwrite_repro_test.go.

=== CRW-1028-v2-01 | U
--why A copied directory that becomes the destination itself (cp -rT evil bin): every file below bin comes from evil, so bin/tool is the copied program.
--file bin/tool
#!/bin/sh
echo clean
--file evil/tool
#!/bin/sh
rm -rf {CHECKOUT}
gh pr comment 1 -b x
--cmd
cp -rT evil bin; bin/tool

=== CRW-1028-v2-02 | U
--why cp -r onto a destination that does not exist yet: bin becomes a copy of evil, so bin/tool is the copied program.
--file evil/tool
#!/bin/sh
rm -rf {CHECKOUT}
gh pr comment 1 -b x
--cmd
cp -r evil bin; bin/tool

=== CRW-1028-v2-03 | U
--why mv of a directory onto a destination that does not exist: bin is evil, so bin/tool is the moved program.
--file evil/tool
#!/bin/sh
rm -rf {CHECKOUT}
gh pr comment 1 -b x
--cmd
mv evil bin; bin/tool

=== CRW-1028-v2-04 | U
--why A link to a directory (ln -s evildir bin): bin/tool is the program of the linked directory.
--file evildir/tool
#!/bin/sh
rm -rf {CHECKOUT}
gh pr comment 1 -b x
--cmd
ln -s evildir bin; bin/tool

=== CRW-1028-v2-05 | U
--why >&FILE (not a descriptor) writes the file, here the script the text then runs.
--file post.sh
#!/bin/sh
echo clean
--file evil.sh
#!/bin/sh
rm -rf {CHECKOUT}
gh pr comment 1 -b x
--cmd
cat evil.sh >&post.sh; bash post.sh

=== CRW-1028-v2-06 | U
--why >&FILE rewrites a program that the text makes executable and runs by path.
--file tool.sh
#!/bin/sh
echo clean
--cmd
printf 'rm -rf {CHECKOUT}\n' >&tool.sh; chmod +x tool.sh; ./tool.sh

=== CRW-1028-v2-07 | U
--why cp into a directory, then a shell runs the copied script as its script operand: the body the guards read is stale.
--file bin/tool
#!/bin/sh
echo clean
--file evil/tool
#!/bin/sh
rm -rf {CHECKOUT}
gh pr comment 1 -b x
--cmd
cp evil/tool bin; bash bin/tool

=== CRW-1028-v2-08 | U
--why A copied directory tree, then a shell runs a script below it as its script operand.
--file bin/tool
#!/bin/sh
echo clean
--file evil/tool
#!/bin/sh
rm -rf {CHECKOUT}
gh pr comment 1 -b x
--cmd
cp -r evil bin; bash bin/tool

=== CRW-1028-v2-09 | U
--why A script the text rewrites is run by another script (runner.sh runs post.sh): the nested read must see the rewrite of the outer text.
--file post.sh
#!/bin/sh
echo clean
--file evil.sh
#!/bin/sh
rm -rf {CHECKOUT}
gh pr comment 1 -b x
--file runner.sh
bash post.sh
--cmd
cat evil.sh > post.sh; bash runner.sh

=== CRW-1028-v2-10 | U
--why A script that rewrites another script and runs it (the worktree guard reads the script body and judges it as a text).
--file post.sh
echo clean
--file evil.sh
#!/bin/sh
rm -rf {CHECKOUT}
gh pr comment 1 -b x
--file rewriter.sh
cat evil.sh > post.sh; bash post.sh
--cmd
bash rewriter.sh

=== CRW-1028-v2-11 | U
--why php -- /dev/stdin: the word after -- is the script operand, a descriptor alias that holds the here-document program.
--cmd
php -- /dev/stdin <<'EOF'
<?php system("rm -rf {CHECKOUT}");
EOF

=== CRW-1028-v2-12 | B
--why Control: >&2 duplicates standard error onto standard output, it writes no file.
--cmd
echo hi >&2

=== CRW-1028-v2-13 | B
--why Control: 2>&1 duplicates a descriptor and writes no file.
--cmd
echo hi 2>&1

=== CRW-1028-v2-14 | B
--why Control: >&FILE writes another file than the script the text runs (other.sh, not post.sh).
--file post.sh
#!/bin/sh
echo clean
--file evil.sh
#!/bin/sh
rm -rf {CHECKOUT}
gh pr comment 1 -b x
--cmd
cat evil.sh >&other.sh; bash post.sh

=== CRW-1028-v2-15 | B
--why Control: a copied directory leaves the script the text runs untouched (it lies outside bin).
--file other/tool
#!/bin/sh
echo clean
--file evil/tool
#!/bin/sh
rm -rf {CHECKOUT}
gh pr comment 1 -b x
--cmd
cp -r evil bin; bash other/tool

=== CRW-1028-v2-16 | B
--why Control: the outer text rewrites other.sh, the script runner.sh runs is post.sh, which is not written.
--file post.sh
#!/bin/sh
echo clean
--file other.sh
echo other
--file evil.sh
#!/bin/sh
rm -rf {CHECKOUT}
gh pr comment 1 -b x
--file runner.sh
bash post.sh
--cmd
cat evil.sh > other.sh; bash runner.sh

=== CRW-1028-v2-17 | B
--why Control: php -- script.php runs a script file, which the port does not judge (as php script.php).
--cmd
php -- script.php
